All four Guide Unit 5 bullet topics (:269-273) are directly covered: U5-01 (Learner-centred literacy instruction) in Topic 5.1; U5-02 (Inquiry-based and project-based learning) in Topic 5.1; U5-03 (Integration of ICT in literacy teaching) in Topic 5.2; U5-04 (Assessment and evaluation of literacy skills) in Topic 5.2.

minott-2011-critical (Minott, 2011): Used in Topic 5.1 (topic-01.mdx:49-57) for teacher tasks in a critical reading classroom (time for judgement, guiding evaluations, questioning, multiple viewpoints, journals); honest declaration that text was read from Semantic Scholar abstract due to repository HTTP 403.

gasque-2016-inquiry (Gasque, 2016): Full text read from SciELO Wayback Machine PDF; supports Dewey's 4 conditions (topic-01.mdx:85-92), research project parts adapted into 7 inquiry stages (topic-01.mdx:94-110), information literacy definition, Harada & Yoshina's 8 features, Yu et al. finding on ICT vs IL (topic-02.mdx:77), and continuous assessment in projects (topic-02.mdx:126).

hafifah-2020-ict (Hafifah & Sulistyo, 2020): Full text read from DergiPark PDF; accurately cites survey of 280 Indonesian lecturers, training/frequency correlations, facilities/training/support barriers (topic-02.mdx:42-47), and technology taking on teacher roles; notes context is Indonesian higher education with cautious application to Pakistan.

rti-2016-egra (RTI International, 2016): Full text read from USAID/RTI PDF; accurately cites assessment continuum (examinations, surveys, classroom assessments) after Kanjee (2009), low-stakes classroom purpose (topic-02.mdx:90), EGRA oral individual format, subtasks, and explicit warnings that no single instrument measures all reading skills and that oral assessments complement written tests (topic-02.mdx:92, 122).
All instructional examples (Mr Akbar, Ms Rubina, Mr Sajjad, Ms Hina, Zainab, Bilal) are clearly presented as original hypothetical teaching cases without statistical claims.

Complete coverage of all 4 sub-topics across Topic 5.1 and Topic 5.2: U5-01 (Learner-centred literacy instruction), U5-02 (Inquiry-based and project-based learning), U5-03 (Integration of ICT in literacy teaching), U5-04 (Assessment and evaluation of literacy skills).

Rigorous execution of the standard 9-part learning cycle in both topics: real classroom situation, explanation with worked examples and misconception correction, activity with group guidance and timing, check your understanding (5 retrieval items), summary, self-assessment checklist, practicum school task, summative task with mini-rubric, and further reading.

Word count and reading time: index.mdx (462 words, 3 min), topic-01.mdx (2,700 words, 15 min), topic-02.mdx (2,910 words, 16 min), unit-assessment.mdx (3,740 words, 20 min), unit-teacher-notes.mdx (750 words, 4 min). Appropriate vocabulary, syntactic simplicity, and accessible tone for HSC/intermediate graduates without prior specialist academic pedagogy training.

Authentic Pakistani classroom and community context grounding (Mirpurkhas government school, safe drinking water inquiry, Sukkur bazaar signs project, Hyderabad private school projector, Badin village school offline phone, Thatta school without internet, Zainab and Bilal reading records).

Specific misconceptions systematically identified and refuted in both topics: learner-centred means the teacher does nothing; project work is only for science; ICT integration means showing slides; a written test is the only way to assess reading.

Practicum school tasks provide ethical observation guidance (five-minute interval mapping of teacher vs pupil talk; conducting a 50-word reading record with cooperating teacher permission and pupil privacy respected).
Comprehensive teacher notes provided (unit-teacher-notes.mdx) covering sequencing, discussion prompts with likely wrong answers, misconception handling, and practical work guidelines.

findings.message: Teaching case illustrations and hypothetical examples: Fictional classroom scenarios (Mr Akbar, Ms Rubina, Mr Sajjad, Ms Hina, Zainab, Bilal) are original instructional examples designed for pedagogy and do not represent empirical case studies or official school inspection records.

Headless review tooling constraint: The crew job brief explicitly prohibits running npm run build, a dev server, or Playwright Chromium. Visual, structural, and presentation checks were conducted within permitted host resources via measure-figure-text.mjs (all 8 SVG variants exit 0 with zero overflow or collision), static heading and table container analysis, and Sharp PNG rasterization with CSS variables resolved.

Abstract-level citation for Minott (2011): The publisher full text returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-02, so citations are strictly limited to findings and teacher tasks reported in the published abstract retrieved via Semantic Scholar.

Mapped reading context for Hafifah & Sulistyo (2020): The study surveyed Indonesian higher education lecturers; lessons are cautiously applied to Pakistani primary and middle school literacy contexts with explicit recognition of contextual differences.
